Sam (People Ops): thanks everyone — dropping the live Q&A thread for leadership. ask anything about mission, positioning, roadmap, competitors and we'll answer here. we’ll start in ~10 but feel free to drop q's now :wave:

Maya (Growth): are we still leaning into 'inference as a differentiator' messaging for market? curious how that plays with product-led growth.

Emily (CEO): short answer: yes. long answer: our narrative is 'shipping predictable, cost-efficient inference at scale' — that resonates with engineers and platform teams. PLG helps signal product quality; enterprise commits follow when predictability and SLAs matter.

Raj (Solutions): can you give a concrete example we should use with prospects?

Emily (CEO): sure — "we reduce tail latency variance and lower per-token costs via batching+cache, so revenue features like chat and embeddings become cheaper to operate than running on raw cloud endpoints." use numbers from Console benchmarks where possible.

Aisha (VP Product): adding: highlight Dedicated for predictable throughput and Private for compliance. both are key hooks for mid-market/enterprise.

Maya (Growth): how hard should we swing at platform teams vs. AI-native startups?

Emily (CEO): both. GTM: PLG motion captures AI-native startups and prototypes; targeted GTM (SEs, Solutions) for platform teams and regulated customers. volume and telemetry usually dictate when we engage sales.

Javier (CTO): from a technical POV, emphasize two things: 1) our runtime choices (continuous batching, KV caching, optimized kernels) reduce P99 latency without sacrificing throughput, and 2) our model catalog + quantization profiles give predictable cost/perf tradeoffs. those are tangible hooks for infra teams.

Maya (Growth): competitors question: how do we position vs. big cloud providers that also offer model endpoints?

Emily (CEO): don't fight on feature parity. we compete on economics, predictability, and deployment flexibility. big clouds win on scale and convenience; we win when customers need consistent latency, lower unit costs, or private deployments with fine-grained control. mention success stories where we replaced a cloud endpoint and cut cost/latency by X — use anonymized metrics.

Raj (Solutions): prospects ask about vendor lock-in. quick answer?

Aisha (VP Product): we promote model portability: customers can pin model versions, export configs, and run Private with the same API. that lowers lock-in risk. also emphasize open model support.

Maya (Growth): roadmap ask: any big bet this year that changes our story?

Emily (CEO): two bets: 1) Redwood Optimize to give automated, workload-specific cost/perf recommendations (that makes switching ROI obvious), and 2) expanding Private (VPC + on-prem) with tighter KMS/HSM integrations for regulated customers. both directly impact sales velocity.

Javier (CTO): technical roadmap note: we're investing in accelerator-specific kernels and smarter routing so customers can get consistent P50/P99 across regions and hardware types. that decreases surprise regressions during rollouts.

Maya (Growth): do we have a simple elevator pitch for customers worried about model quality after quantization?

Aisha (VP Product): yes: "We run quantization-aware evals on your representative prompts and propose model+quantization pairs that meet quality thresholds while reducing cost." point them to the evals deck and examples.

Sam (People Ops): quick ops note — recording this thread, will pull highlights into the all-hands follow-up doc.

DevDeployBot: deploy job 5123 finished: all-hands slides uploaded to https://internal.redwood/s3/all-hands/mar-2026.pdf :white_check_mark:

Emily (CEO): thanks all for the questions. if anyone wants deeper follow-ups ping me or Aisha — we'll schedule product+sales office hours next week to help craft blinded case studies and updated one-pagers.

Maya (Growth): thank you! will send a calendar invite for office hours. :raised_hands:

Raj (Solutions): adding a note to the sales playbook with the P99/Cost bullets.

Javier (CTO): happy to join office hours for technical Q&A.

Sam (People Ops): great thread — closing in ~1h, drop any last q's. :lock:
